justification.mechanism: Small reservoirs store runoff: hill reservoirs in the Merguellil basin in Tunisia were modelled to reduce outlet flows by 13%, and users of small reservoirs in northern Ghana list limiting rainy-season floods among their benefits [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1].
justification.conditionality: The Tunisian figure is modelled and the Ghana finding is user perception, not a measured flood reduction [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. Size and siting can reverse the effect: larger sand dams increase the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage, and check dams can cause channel incision downstream, observed at 81% of surveyed check dams in a Spanish catchment [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1].

mitigation_mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and banquettes slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces cut mean runoff by 50 to 98% and flood peaks on small mountain plots, a global study of 105 cases finds terraces on average 2.5 times more effective than slopes at reducing runoff, stone bunds lower hillslope peak discharges, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment clipped peak discharges and cut runoff volume by 50% [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_runoff_reduction_willem21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2]. Compacted hill terraces with retention walls in Uttarakhand are credited with limiting damage from landslides and flood [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].
caveats: Diversion banquettes and ditches, filed in this family, do the opposite: in Niger they doubled the runoff coefficient, raised peak discharges and increased gully and bank erosion, and ditches with a downslope bank accelerate runoff and concentration time [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Abandoned terraces increase erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or never maintained, catchment-level peak-flow evidence is scarce, and most units measure runoff or soil loss as proxies for flood impact [ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1]. The Rwanda sediment figures and the Uttarakhand claim are Bank self-reports, and the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2].
